title: Illness in 1943 and his 1956 operation
summary: Williams reflects on friends dying, his sickness in 1943 and surviving an operation in 1956.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Is he dead? Oh, he's dead. That's why I was thinking a couple weeks ago, all the people I knew, they were dead. When I was sick in 43, fellas come on Fusher Street, come and buy my home. I told my wife, I said, don't sell the home, I might play the game. So she didn't sell the home. In 1944, I played over in Coverture, this big fellow that he died last year. He's a bass player in the Tramont Club too. Dan Moody. Dan Moody, I played with him. So the sick is going to die.
No. You don't know though. You can't tell. You never can tell. Yeah, sure was quick, you know, the way he came for red clock.

And this other boy come quick. I knew he was coming quick. Yeah, yeah. I was with him that afternoon. Yeah. Well, see when the clock stopped beating, she stopped giving me the time. Well, my heart put a good show for us. When I got operated on in 56, I was 60, near 66. The doctor told me, he said, we done examined you all over your sins as a man, 59 years old. And he said, you can go through that operation, you're going to make it. I made it. That also operation. Also? Yeah. Made that operation. So I'm doing for the good now.
